You are the decoding-software team on NeuroForge Bio. Working copy: C:\Users\mariu\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-mariu\8f3352b3-40ab-4151-abc9-d1de1978973c\scratchpad\neuroforge\ . Read scratchpad\neuroforge-techlead-brief.md and neuroforge-benchmark.md first. The Rust core is `core/nf-core` and decoders live there and in research/code. Honesty: pre-product, research/simulation only, no medical claims, no fabricated numbers; MEASURE before/after; don't change decoder math without a parity test. Be mindful of RAM (16 GB box); build to scratchpad\nf-target-sw (CARGO_TARGET_DIR), offline/locked, no new crates without posting an audit note first.

IMPLEMENT the owner's engineering requirements (deterministic low-jitter real-time decoding). Scope honestly: implement what's tractable in Rust now, and write a clear design note for what needs more. Priorities:
1. DECOUPLE STREAMING FROM INFERENCE: a lock-free / bounded SPSC ring buffer between an ingestion producer and the inference consumer, so inference never blocks ingestion and vice-versa. Pre-allocate all buffers; ZERO heap allocations in the hot decode loop (verify with an allocation counter in a test). No GC (Rust), pinned/`spin_sleep`-free deterministic tick.
2. SELF-CONTAINED PIPELINE ARTIFACT: a single serializable artifact that bundles causal filter state + thresholding/binning params + spike/feature transforms + the model weights, so preprocessing can never drift from the model. Define the struct, (de)serialize it, and a loader that reconstructs the exact streaming pipeline. Add a test that the artifact reproduces identical output to the training-config path (no train/serve skew).
3. ROBUSTNESS TO NON-STATIONARITY: an online baseline-recalibration hook and a manifold-alignment step (Procrustes / simple domain-adaptation) that can re-align features WITHOUT interrupting the control loop. Simulate electrode drift (shifting/vanishing units, baseline change) and show the recalibration recovers accuracy; measure the cost.
4. MEASURE: per-step latency AND jitter (p99/max) for the streaming path vs the current batch path, on synthetic data, same machine; show the ring-buffer/pre-allocation removes allocation-driven spikes.
Write code in core/nf-core (new modules; keep existing tests green), add unit tests, and a report to scratchpad\neuroforge-decoding-sw.md with what was implemented, measured latency/jitter before/after, parity results, and what's deferred. Return a concise summary. No medical/clinical claims.

handback.t:
DONE. Report: scratchpad\neuroforge-decoding-sw.md. Design/deferred note: neuroforge\docs\design\rt-decoding.md. Everything is RESEARCH ONLY, SYNTHETIC data, no clinical claims.

CODE (all new, in neuroforge\core\nf-core): src\rt\{ring,tick,artifact,pipeline,offline,align,linalg,synth,sim,stats,mod}.rs; tests\rt_parity.rs, rt_alloc.rs, rt_drift.rs, rt_fixtures\; examples\rt_bench.rs, rt_drift_sim.rs. Existing files touched: lib.rs (`pub mod rt;` + doc row) and core\nf-core\Cargo.toml (serde_json `float_roundtrip` FEATURE only; no new crate, Cargo.lock unchanged).

IMPLEMENTED
1. Safe-Rust (no unsafe) lock-free SPSC ring, pre-allocated, non-blocking push/pop. Spin TickClock with a fixed schedule (no sleep, no crate). Streaming pipeline (biquad, threshold, binning, features, EMA, alignment, lag history, ridge or Kalman). Counting-allocator test: 0 allocations over ~35.7k frames of ring push/pop + decode, including EMA and a live alignment commit; the negative control shows the counter works (28 allocations on the whole-array path).
2. PipelineArtifact (serde JSON, validating loader, sha256 id) rebuilds the exact streaming pipeline. The streaming output equals the independently written whole-array training-config path BIT-FOR-BIT (ridge; with EMA + dense alignment). Kalman through the full chain matches to 1e-12. A teeth test shows a changed threshold or filter is detected. The skew test caught a real bug: default serde_json round-trips some f64 one ulp off; fixed with float_roundtrip.
3. Online baseline EMA (warm-started) and a seqlock live-parameter stage: Procrustes alignment is fitted in the background and published to the running pipeline with bounded, optionally chunked, per-bin work and no skipped bins.
4. Parity vs the Python reference (fixtures from m1lib + scipy): ridge, Kalman step, Procrustes, biquad all pass at 1e-9 to 1e-12.

MEASURED (N=96, 20 ms bins, 3 runs, shared box)
- Per-bin compute, streaming vs a benchmark-written allocating comparator with identical outputs: p50 48-51 us vs 106-119 us (~2.1x); p95 ~2.7x. Under a heap-churn thread the allocating path's p99 goes from 207-241 to 413-567 us, while the streaming p50/p95 stay put. Allocations per bin: 0 vs 198.
- CAVEAT: the machine was at 100% CPU from other processes. A bare clock loop lost 11-24% of wall time to stalls up to 23-35 ms. So p99.9, max and the end-to-end tails (8-90 ms) are OS scheduling for BOTH paths. I cannot claim the ring removes allocation-driven tail spikes on this box.
- Ring vs mpsc+Vec end to end: both have p50 ~1 us, 0 drops. The ring absorbed consumer stalls of up to ~120 ms (high-water 726/1024) without blocking the producer. No latency advantage is visible; the benefit is structural.
- Recalibration cost: EMA ~0 us; dense 96x96 alignment ~+7 us/bin; commit tick +6-12 us (about 0 when chunked); background fit ~50 ms at N=96.

DRIFT SIM (synthetic, R2)
- Combined drift, holdout seeds: stale decoder 0.46 mean (one seed 0.11) -> EMA + Procrustes 0.86 (whitened 0.88; label-retrain ceiling 0.93). Baseline-only, vanishing-only and shifting-only scenarios also gain on average, but alignment can HURT under mild drift (worst per seed -0.03, and -0.13 on a dev seed), so a gate is needed.
- The calibration trajectory must cover the latent space: with a slow one (rho 0.98) the same fit overfit and fell below stale. An EMA at alpha 0.01 destroyed the signal; the shipped alpha is 0.0005.
- Config was fixed a priori and confirmed on 4 holdout seeds.

DEFERRED (details in the design note)
- OS determinism: core isolation, RT priority, mlockall/MMCSS, dedicated rig.
- Hardware timestamps and clock-drift tracking; a loop-back closed-loop latency rig.
- Real-data replay (M1/MC_RTT) through the artifact; GRU in the zero-alloc loop.
- Label-free alignment; a drift detector that gates alignment.
- Online threshold/scale recalibration; signed artifact rollout; SIMD/fixed-point kernels.

ENVIRONMENT ISSUES
- `cargo test -p nf-core` cannot build here (pre-existing: proptest -> getrandom 0.3 needs dlltool/as on windows-gnu). I ran all tests in a scratch mirror at scratchpad\nf-sw (sync.sh) without proptest. Green: 61 lib tests (43 existing + 18 new), existing vectors.rs (5), rt_parity 10, rt_alloc 2, rt_drift 2, in both release and debug (rt lib/parity/alloc). Clippy: 0 warnings. hw-guard: 526 files clean.
- NOT re-run, needs proptest, please run in CI: tests\props.rs, vectors_v2.rs, tests\stream.rs, and lib tests with --features stream. `cargo build --features stream` succeeds.
- Orphan process: an unfiltered `find /` I started while looking for dlltool (PID 34824) is still burning ~1 core. I tried Stop-Process but it was denied, so I left it. Please end it manually. It adds to the benchmark noise (other heavy non-mine processes also saturate the CPU).
- One of my own runaway debug test processes was stopped via TaskStop; the test was fixed (it livelocked by design under load).
